known_defects: v1 content extent is exactly 77 columns - the pane width - so there is zero horizontal margin; --check and the live header both report a fit, but a 76-column pane would overflow.

The trunk splits at two junction points (one spur per branch) because the renderer's trunk geometry is 'one corridor plus one spur per branch'; the user's literal 'split in exactly one spot' is approximated, not achieved.
v1 draws two paths into Compute BMC and into Power shelf (OOB physical reach plus the rms API call). That duplication is intentional (reach vs API) but it is the densest part of the frame.
v1 is 77x24: it uses half the 47 rows, leaving a large empty area below the graph (which is also where the control palette floats).
v2 is 33x37: it uses 33 of 77 columns, so the right half of the pane is empty and no zoom-in is available.
Group names are not rendered as text; plane identity is carried by node labels and hue only.
The string 'Redfish/HTTPS' is the label of two distinct edges (e2, e3) because the source names one protocol for two device classes; each label is anchored to its own edge.
Node labels 'Compute BMC' and 'Power shelf' lose the tray count and the CDU/PDU endpoints.

blockers.detail: trunks draw one corridor plus one spur per branch (junction per spur); a single Y-junction for three branches cannot be expressed. Closest honest subset used.
no field draws 'does not connect'; OOB !-> DCGM and 'OOB carries no training/storage/NVLink' are expressed by absence plus this report.
group names never appear on screen, so the four-plane split is legible only from node labels and hue.

the case needs 13 nodes and --check warns above 12, so one overview of all four planes is impossible without dropping required nodes; the split into v1/v2 with a coverage map is the compliant response.
